> **Pipeline step 03 — fork-length diagnostics (supporting).**
>
> **Purpose.** Every fork-length model flagged the DHARMa uniformity (KS) test. This notebook
> refits the best model (fit 9) under alternative response families and a heteroscedastic
> variant to test whether the misfit is a distributional-shape problem. Result: it is not —
> see `fit9_bimodality_diagnosis.Rmd`.
>
> **Inputs.** `data/tps_forklength_data.csv`, `fits_tps_fl_kfold/fit_tps_fl_9.rds`.
> **Outputs.** alternative-family fits and DHARMa / pp_check panels under `fits_tps_fl_kfold/`.

```{r project-root, include=FALSE}
# Every path in this notebook (data/, fits_*/, output_figs/, cache/) is relative to the
# REPOSITORY ROOT, not to this file's sub-folder. Walk up from the working directory to the
# folder holding the .Rproj file, and make knitr (and RStudio's chunk-by-chunk notebook
# mode) run every chunk from there. Base R only -- no extra package needed.
find_repo_root <- function(path = getwd()) {
  p <- normalizePath(path)
  while (!length(list.files(p, pattern = "\\.Rproj$"))) {
    if (dirname(p) == p) stop("No .Rproj file found above ", path)
    p <- dirname(p)
  }
  p
}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = find_repo_root())
```
`fit_tps_fl_9` (and every other fit in `tps_forklength_kfold_models.Rmd`'s 1..19 set)
flagged on the DHARMa KS/uniformity test — see
`fits_tps_fl_kfold/DHARMa_diagnostics/fit_tps_fl_dharma_summary.csv` (all 19 fits FLAG on
`ks_flag`, all pass dispersion/outlier/zero-inflation). Dispersion passing but uniformity failing
points at distributional shape (skew / non-constant variance) rather than over/under-dispersion,
so this notebook refits fit 9's predictor set under three alternative response distributions
(lognormal, skew_normal, Gamma) plus a heteroscedastic (`sigma ~ ...`) gaussian variant, and lines
up DHARMa panels + `pp_check` for all four against the original gaussian fit.

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
library(DHARMa)
library(patchwork)
library(kableExtra)

options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())
```

Config.
```{r config}
FIT_DIR      <- "fits_tps_fl_kfold"                         # where fit_tps_fl_9.rds already lives
OUT_DIR      <- file.path(FIT_DIR, "fit9_family_compare")   # new variants + diagnostics go here
if (!dir.exists(OUT_DIR)) dir.create(OUT_DIR, recursive = TRUE)

n_sim_dharma <- 1000   # same as DHARMa_testing.Rmd, for comparable p-values
```

Data — identical to the kfold notebook.
```{r data}
d_fl <- read_csv("data/tps_forklength_data.csv")
d_fl$Edge_Type   <- factor(d_fl$Edge_Type)
d_fl$StationCode <- factor(d_fl$StationCode)
```

Fit 9's fixed-effects string, transcribed from `fit_defs` in
`tidal-parr-forklength-analysis2_kfold.Rmd` (`num == 9`):
`distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z + start_depth_z + out30_z`.
```{r formula}
fit9_fixef <- "distance_along_channel_z + distance_m_z + start_depth_z + out30_z"

mu_rhs   <- paste(fit9_fixef, "+ water_year_day_z + (1|StationCode)")
mu_form  <- as.formula(paste("ForkLength ~", mu_rhs))

# Same weakly-informative prior as the source fit. Note: for the log-link families
# (lognormal, Gamma) this prior applies on the log-response scale, not the raw-mm scale,
# so it is still weakly informative there but not literally "the same" prior in effect.
fl_priors <- c(set_prior("normal(0,5)", class = "b"))

fit_control <- list(max_treedepth = 10, adapt_delta = 0.95)
fit_iter    <- 4000
fit_warmup  <- 2000
fit_chains  <- 4
```

Fit-or-load helper — reruns `brm()` only if the cached `.rds` isn't already on disk, so re-running
this notebook doesn't silently re-trigger a ~4-chain refit.
```{r fit-or-load}
fit_or_load <- function(path, formula_obj, family_obj, ...) {
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    message("Loading cached fit: ", path)
    return(readRDS(path))
  }
  message("Fitting: ", path)
  fit <- brm(
    formula   = formula_obj,
    family    = family_obj,
    data      = d_fl,
    prior     = fl_priors,
    iter      = fit_iter, warmup = fit_warmup, chains = fit_chains,
    control   = fit_control,
    save_pars = save_pars(all = FALSE),
    ...
  )
  saveRDS(fit, path)
  fit
}
```

Refit fit 9 under each alternative. Interactive only — do not knit cold (4 model fits at
iter = 4000 / warmup = 2000 / chains = 4 each).
```{r refit-variants, eval=FALSE}
fit9_lognormal <- fit_or_load(
  file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit_tps_fl_9_lognormal.rds"),
  mu_form, lognormal()
)

fit9_skew <- fit_or_load(
  file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit_tps_fl_9_skew_normal.rds"),
  mu_form, skew_normal()
)

fit9_gamma <- fit_or_load(
  file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit_tps_fl_9_gamma.rds"),
  mu_form, Gamma(link = "log")
)

# Heteroscedastic gaussian: same mean structure, plus a linear model on log(sigma) using
# the same predictor set (minus the station random intercept, to keep the sigma submodel simple).
sigma_rhs  <- paste(fit9_fixef, "+ water_year_day_z")
sigma_form <- bf(mu_form, as.formula(paste("sigma ~", sigma_rhs)))

fit9_sigma <- fit_or_load(
  file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit_tps_fl_9_sigma_model.rds"),
  sigma_form, gaussian()
)
```

Baseline gaussian fit (already fit in the kfold notebook) + the four new variants, as one named
list for looped diagnostics.
```{r assemble}
fit9_gaussian <- readRDS(file.path(FIT_DIR, "fit_tps_fl_9.rds"))

fits9 <- list(
  gaussian     = fit9_gaussian,
  lognormal    = fit9_lognormal,
  skew_normal  = fit9_skew,
  gamma        = fit9_gamma,
  sigma_model  = fit9_sigma
)
```


## DHARMa summary table across variants

Same tests/flags as `DHARMa_testing.Rmd`, run once per variant on identical `n_sim_dharma`
simulations.
```{r dharma-summary, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
pval_flag <- function(p, alpha = 0.05) if (is.na(p) || p < alpha) "FLAG" else "pass"

summarize_dharma <- function(fit, label, n_sim = n_sim_dharma) {
  set.seed(123)
  sim <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = fit, n = n_sim, plot = FALSE)

  t_unif <- testUniformity(sim,    plot = FALSE)
  t_disp <- testDispersion(sim,    plot = FALSE)
  t_out  <- testOutliers(sim,      plot = FALSE, type = "bootstrap")

  tibble(
    fit           = label,
    ks_stat       = round(t_unif$statistic, 4),
    ks_p          = round(t_unif$p.value,   4),
    ks_flag       = pval_flag(t_unif$p.value),
    disp_ratio    = round(t_disp$statistic, 4),
    disp_p        = round(t_disp$p.value,   4),
    disp_flag     = pval_flag(t_disp$p.value),
    outlier_frac  = round(as.numeric(t_out$statistic) / length(sim$scaledResiduals), 4),
    outlier_p     = round(t_out$p.value,   4),
    outlier_flag  = pval_flag(t_out$p.value),
    any_flag      = if (any(c(ks_flag, disp_flag, outlier_flag) == "FLAG")) "FLAG" else "pass"
  )
}

dharma_summary9 <- map2_dfr(fits9, names(fits9), summarize_dharma)

flag_cols <- c("ks_flag", "disp_flag", "outlier_flag", "any_flag")
dharma_summary9 |>
  mutate(across(all_of(flag_cols),
                ~ cell_spec(.x, color = if_else(.x == "FLAG", "red", "black"),
                            bold = .x == "FLAG"))) |>
  knitr::kable(format = "html", escape = FALSE, align = "c") |>
  kableExtra::kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover"))

write_csv(dharma_summary9, file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit_tps_fl_9_family_compare_dharma_summary.csv"))
```


## DHARMa panels, side by side

One row per variant: QQ-uniform plot + residuals-vs-predicted, the two plots that speak most
directly to the original "bad QQplot" flag. Saved as one combined PNG plus rendered inline.
```{r dharma-panels, fig.width=9, fig.height=16, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
png(file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit_tps_fl_9_family_compare_qq_resid.png"),
    width = 1600, height = 2800, res = 200)
par(mfrow = c(length(fits9), 2), oma = c(0, 1, 2, 1))
for (label in names(fits9)) {
  set.seed(123)
  sim <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = fits9[[label]], n = n_sim_dharma, plot = FALSE)
  plotQQunif(sim, main = paste(label, "- QQ"))
  plotResiduals(sim, main = paste(label, "- resid vs pred"))
}
mtext("fit 9 — family / sigma-model comparison", outer = TRUE, cex = 1.2)
dev.off()

par(mfrow = c(length(fits9), 2), oma = c(0, 1, 2, 1))
for (label in names(fits9)) {
  set.seed(123)
  sim <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = fits9[[label]], n = n_sim_dharma, plot = FALSE)
  plotQQunif(sim, main = paste(label, "- QQ"))
  plotResiduals(sim, main = paste(label, "- resid vs pred"))
}
mtext("fit 9 — family / sigma-model comparison", outer = TRUE, cex = 1.2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

Full 2x2 DHARMa panel (QQ, resid-vs-fitted, dispersion, zero-inflation) per variant, saved
individually — same layout as `DHARMa_testing.Rmd`'s batch diagnostics.
```{r dharma-2x2-each, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
for (label in names(fits9)) {
  set.seed(123)
  sim <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = fits9[[label]], n = n_sim_dharma, plot = FALSE)

  png(file.path(OUT_DIR, paste0("fit_tps_fl_9_", label, "_2x2.png")),
      width = 1800, height = 1400, res = 200)
  par(mfrow = c(2, 2), oma = c(0, 1, 2, 1))
  plotQQunif(sim)
  plotResiduals(sim)
  testDispersion(sim)
  testZeroInflation(sim)
  mtext(paste("fit_tps_fl_9 —", label), outer = TRUE, cex = 1.2)
  par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
  dev.off()
}
```


## pp_check, side by side

`pp_check()` (density overlay of observed vs. posterior-predicted `ForkLength`) for each variant,
arranged in a grid for direct comparison.
```{r pp-check-grid, fig.width=10, fig.height=10, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
pp_plots <- imap(fits9, function(fit, label) {
  pp_check(fit, ndraws = 100) +
    ggtitle(label) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
})

pp_grid <- wrap_plots(pp_plots, ncol = 2) +
  plot_annotation(title = "fit 9 — pp_check by family / sigma-model variant")
pp_grid

ggsave(file.path(OUT_DIR, "fit_tps_fl_9_family_compare_pp_check.png"),
       pp_grid, width = 10, height = 10, dpi = 200)
```
